title: Counsel
summary: An agent in the app, on a model from OpenRouter: it reads the app's data, changes it when asked, and keeps each conversation as a chat of its own.
description:
The agent works in the app the way a professional would beside the user: it knows what the app holds and can act in it. Each product that uses this part says what the agent's profession is (a coach, a tutor), what the app's data is, and which actions the agent may take.

The agent runs on the user's own OpenRouter account, so the user chooses the model and pays for it.
groundwork: The app has settings the user can open, and a part can add a section of its own to them.

groundwork.text: The app keeps its data in a SQLite database that can be opened a second time, read-only, while the app uses it.
ways: a second connection to the same file, opened read-only
a second connection with `PRAGMA query_only` set

groundwork.text: The app's database schema changes only through migrations, and a part can add migrations of its own for its tables.
ways: the migrations the app already runs at startup, in a folder a part can add to
a migration runner that takes migrations from several modules, in a fixed order

groundwork.text: Every change a user can make from the app's screens goes through code that can also be called from outside the screen, with the same checks.
ways: the functions the screens already call to save
the screens' writes moved into one module of commands that the screens and the agent both call

groundwork.text: The app knows, in a form its code can read, which screen the user has open and which item is on it, and can open any screen or item by that form.
ways: the router's current route and its parameters
a store of the current selection beside the router

groundwork.text: The app has a place for a chat that stays open beside the screen the user is on.
ways: a side panel the screens make room for
a drawer that slides over the screen on narrow windows

stories.as: someone who keeps their records in the app
stories.want: to ask about them in plain words
stories.soThat: I get an answer without digging through screens

stories.as: someone in the middle of something
stories.want: to tell the app what to change
stories.soThat: it's done without my finding the screen for it

stories.as: someone who comes with a different question each time
stories.want: each conversation to be one of its own that I can come back to
stories.soThat: an old topic doesn't muddle a new one

stories.as: someone paying for the model myself
stories.want: to bring my own key and choose the model
stories.soThat: I decide what I pay for and what I get

stories.as: someone using an app for one part of my life
stories.want: the agent to meet me as someone in that field would
stories.soThat: its help fits what I came to the app for

requirements.text: Until an API key is saved and a model chosen, the chat says which is missing and leads to the settings for it.
The user can stop the agent at any point of an answer; what it wrote so far stays in the chat, and so do changes it already made.

history.text: The user can stop the agent at any point of an answer; what it wrote so far stays in the chat, and so do changes it already made, with their undo.

requirements.text: The agent makes at most `counsel.max-steps` tool calls for one answer, then answers with what it found.

A request to OpenRouter that fails says why in plain words, telling apart a key that isn't accepted, credit that has run out, a rate limit, a model that isn't available and no network, and says what to do about it.
An answer the agent is working on keeps going when the screen turns off or the user switches to another app, for as long as the platform allows.
When the platform ends an answer anyway, the chat says the answer was cut off, keeps what was written and changed so far, and offers to continue.

values.description: How many tool calls the agent may make for one answer.
